findings.text: follow-on: _dispose_the_figure_finding answers the finding by writing the disposition through review.store_review directly rather than through crew dispose, which the plan's done-when names. crew dispose cannot reach a figure finding today: its selection excludes figure records by rubric (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:140-144 nulls a stored record whose rubric is figure, and :150-152 does the same to the newest fallback), and review_dispositions.record_finding_disposition (reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py:438) calls review.stored_record with no rubric, whose rubric=None predicate (reckon/crew/review.py:2159-2160) returns only non-figure records. So the guard's 'a disposed finding no longer refuses' half is asserted against a hand-written disposition, not the production disposal route; the worker recorded this as a follow-on and was fenced out of the peer's recovery_review_subject.py path.

follow-on: _newest_figure_review swallows OSError and ValueError and returns None, so an unreadable figure-review record (for example malformed JSON in the store) makes the guard report no finding and the promotion proceeds. The guard exists because a figure review otherwise protects nothing, and a store it cannot read is exactly the case where a blocking finding could sit unreported; returning None makes the new refusal fail open in the class of defect it was added to close. No test covers the unreadable-store branch.
